title: Creation Week
summary: God creates the heavens and the earth and all that is in them in six days and rests on the seventh.
description: Genesis 1:1–2:3. Adam and Eve are created on the sixth day; God rests on the seventh day and sanctifies it.

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 4: Dating Creation and the Deluge," ARJ 16 (2023): 475–489, section "AP-30: Creation: 4004 B.C."
chronologies.note: Also CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones): "4004 Creation of Mankind".

chronologies.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 1: Problem, Data, and Methodology," ARJ 15 (2022): 377–390, section "Our Assumptions (Declared Biases)", Table 1 "Biblically derived dates from Ussher and Jones"
chronologies.note: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones biblical baseline adopted by CFAH); not a triangulated anchor point.

chronologies.citation: Floyd Nolen Jones, Chart No. 1 "Creation to Jesus Christ" (© 1993), line "0 AM 4004 BC year of CREATION"; also Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), Chart One §B, p. 26 ("2348 + 1656 = 4004 BC")
chronologies.note: Jones counts Creation as 0 AM (Ussher uses AM 1).

chronologies.date: Six days, God resting on the seventh
chronologies.note: Scripture states the six-day duration; no absolute year.

chronologies.date: 1 AM, 710 JP, 4004 BC; evening preceding Sunday 23 Oct to Saturday 29 Oct (Julian)
chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, First Age, §1–8
Jordan, "Egypt in Biblical History," Biblical Chronology 5:8 (December 1993), chart "Anno Mundi / B.C. (SBC) / B.C. (CCC)" at the start of the article
chronologies.note: B.C. year is Jordan's "SBC" (strictest Biblical chronology), which takes Daniel's 70 weeks literally from Cyrus (456 B.C. instead of the conventional 536 B.C.); not comparable one-to-one with Ussher/CFAH B.C. years. Same chart: CCC "undated". Pentateuch Part 2 (BC 6:4) year list also begins "0 - Adam created".

chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 11, chart table "Biblical History According To A.M & B.C. Dates"
chronologies.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 0. The compilation's B.C. year (4010) is AM subtracted from 4010 (its own convention: Creation 4010 B.C.); Jordan's own SBC B.C. figures differ (here 3930 B.C.). Display only; never converted or used for sorting.
Epoch of the AM count by definition.

chronologies.citation: Taking the World for Jesus, ch. 1 "The Roman Empire and the Men Who Turned the World Upside Down", PDF p. 14 (printed pp. 27–28)
chronologies.note: Printed as a round figure ("from 4000 BC to AD 30"). Differs from the sort year (4004 BC, cfah-anchor) by 4 years.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 1 "Creation and the Global Flood", PDF p. 16 (printed p. 15)
chronologies.note: The book's own chronology. Timeline Review pairs it with an asterisked 4004 BC (the book's Ussher-chronology equivalent). (pp. 42, 78). End note 1 (p. 526) explains the long chronology. Differs from the sort year (4004 BC, cfah-anchor) by 170 years.
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "4,004 BC" (PDF p. 21): 170 years later.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 1 "The Song of Creation", PDF p. 21 (printed p. 7)
chronologies.note: Derived in the text from 3104 BC plus 900 years; also the heading of ch. I "(4004–3584 BC)" and Timeline Review p. 73.
